html:
Authentication and outbound Email

Email / SMTP is enabled by default; an explicit saved capability selection or exclusion still applies. Enable Authentication to use its standalone administration tools. Configuration lives in Parameter Store. Templates are detached prefills: opening a template does not save a profile, connect an account or send a message.

Configure authorization

Create an OAuth client from an Auth template and save it as work_client. Configure your own registered client ID, the exact provider issuer or HTTPS endpoints, client authentication method, allowed scopes and redirect URI. For browser authorization, register the exact controller URL ending in /api/agent/auth/oauth/callback with the provider. HTTPS is required outside literal loopback development addresses. Entra discovery uses a tenant-specific issuer; replace template placeholders.

Create an OAuth Connection as work_identity. Set client_ref to work_client, choose authorization_code_pkce, device_authorization or client_credentials, and set requested_scopes to the intended subset of the client's allowlist. Client secrets, private keys, refresh tokens and access tokens remain private Parameter Store fields. They are never needed in a prompt or an Email tool argument.

Use auth.inspect for safe identities, auth.connect to authorize, auth.test to validate/refresh, and auth.disconnect to clear authorization and attempt revocation. Authorization can also begin when HTTP or Email first needs it. Click Open authorization page yourself, or complete the displayed device code. The operation waits without model inference, then resumes the same accepted invocation. Stop cancels the wait. After controller restart or expiry, begin a new authorization; old callbacks cannot be replayed. Profile edits invalidate pending authorization and existing leases.

Supported methods are public clients, client secret Basic/Post, client secret JWT, private key JWT and mutual TLS. Browser grants always use S256 PKCE. OIDC validates issuer, signature, audience, timestamps and nonce. Discovery endpoint origins must match the trusted issuer or an explicitly saved allowlist. PAR supports automatic, required and disabled modes. DPoP, JARM, token exchange, RAR and dynamic registration are not supported in this version.

Configure an Email sender

For Gmail, including Google-hosted custom domains, you can save one Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP) JSON template and use its Parameter Store reference as Email's profile_key and Gmail's account_ref. Follow Gmail app-password setup. Email derives the fixed Gmail SMTP settings privately from this account; it creates no second credential record. email.accounts reports it as configured, and email.test_connection tests SMTP without sending a message. Google requires 2-Step Verification to create an app password; no OAuth application is needed for this option. Existing password and OAuth SMTP profiles continue to work.

Create an Email / SMTP profile, for example research_mail. Set SMTP host/port, TLS mode and fixed from_email. Optional from_name, reply_to and envelope_from are profile-owned; the model cannot override them. Choose one authentication form:

  • none: an explicitly configured relay; plaintext is permitted only here.
  • password: saved username/password over STARTTLS or implicit TLS.
  • oauth2: mailbox username, auth_ref pointing to work_identity, SASL mechanism and required scopes. Email obtains credentials exclusively through Auth.

STARTTLS fails if the server does not advertise or successfully negotiate it. Certificate verification defaults to system trust; a saved custom CA is supported. Explicit insecure verification reports a warning. Both password and OAuth require verified encrypted controller-to-Gateway transport before credentials are released. SMTP DNS/connections and Email's OAuth discovery, token, refresh and callback exchanges run on the selected Gateway, including private network endpoints reachable only there. Use email.connect to authorize through that Gateway. The controller hosts the browser callback and owns token persistence; it does not contact Email's token endpoint itself. An unavailable, changed or unsupported Gateway fails without a local fallback. Older Gateways must be updated to advertise email_smtp and serve the private Email operation route.

The Microsoft delegated presets use smtp.office365.com:587, STARTTLS, XOAUTH2, https://outlook.office.com/SMTP.Send and offline_access. The separate app-only presets use client credentials and https://outlook.office365.com/.default. App-only setup requires administrator consent, SMTP.SendAsApp, an Exchange service principal and mailbox sending permissions. SMTO does not grant these permissions automatically. See Microsoft SMTP OAuth and SMTP submission settings.

The Google template uses smtp.gmail.com:587, STARTTLS, XOAUTH2 and https://mail.google.com/. This SMTP scope differs from granular Gmail REST scopes; a Gmail REST authorization does not imply SMTP permission. See Google SMTP settings and XOAUTH2 scope and protocol. Provider defaults were checked on 2026-09-30; provider and tenant policies still apply.

Provider presets form three linked Parameter Store records. Save the Email OAuth App client, save its Email OAuth Connection with the matching client_ref, then select that connection as the SMTP sender's auth.auth_ref. Microsoft delegated/app-only, Google SMTP and generic OAuth each have client and connection drafts. Replace tenant, client, secret, callback and sender placeholders before saving. Selecting a draft performs no network request and stores nothing. Password and intentional internal relay profiles need only the SMTP record.

Test and send

Tool Effect and prerequisites
email.accounts Read saved sender identities and authorization readiness; no network.
email.connection_status Read one sender's saved authorization readiness; no network.
email.connect Internal OAuth authorization/refresh through the selected verified Gateway. Password/relay profiles need no consent.
email.test_connection Test selected Gateway SMTP/TLS/authentication without MAIL, RCPT or DATA. May request OAuth consent.
email.send Network-heavy write using normal confirmation or full access.

email.inspect and email.test remain compatible aliases. An accepted sender @parameter promotes Email entry tools within the existing capability policy; it cannot override exclusions. email.send takes profile_key, to, optional cc/bcc, subject, text_body and/or html_body, plus optional attachment objects such as {"ref":"artifact://art_…","filename":"report.pdf"}. Use exact existing artifact or conversation-upload references. Eligible absolute temporary references use the existing selected-Gateway temp-publication rules, including traversal/symlink protections; they do not permit arbitrary controller file reads. Model-provided base64 is not accepted. The conversation must already have access to each artifact/upload. At least one nonblank body is required.

Sending is a write operation and uses normal manual confirmation or full-access policy. Review the fixed sender, separate To/CC/BCC groups, subject, attachment labels (sizes when already available) and bounded plain-text body preview. HTML is represented as text, never rendered by the confirmation preview. The approval binds the saved sender revision; editing it while approval or OAuth is pending invalidates continuation. An authorization wait preserves approval for that invocation. Message bodies are excluded from activity details; the accepted invocation follows normal conversation retention. BCC addresses are envelope recipients only and never enter MIME headers.

The limit is 100 recipient entries and 20 attachments. Total attachment bytes are limited to 20 MiB; final encoded MIME must fit the profile limit (at most 25 MiB) and the server's advertised SIZE. Unicode local parts require SMTPUTF8 and 8BITMIME; Unicode domains use IDNA. Header control characters and unsafe filenames are rejected before sending. Exact bytes are transferred to the Gateway in bounded chunks, verified by size and SHA-256, bound to the run and operation, consumed once, and removed on completion or within ten minutes. Staging is volatile memory, capped at 64 MiB across 128 entries; chunks are at most 256 KiB. No separate mail or authorization database exists.

accepted means the server returned final SMTP 250, not proof of recipient delivery. partially_accepted lists accepted and rejected recipients; repeating the whole send would duplicate mail to accepted recipients. A confirmed SMTP rejection is reported separately. If the connection disappears after message transmission starts and before a valid final reply, or the Gateway returns incomplete/mismatched send evidence, the result is unknown_effect. The runtime blocks automatic resend. Use its deterministic Message-ID to reconcile with server logs or the recipient. Cancellation after DATA cannot undo remote acceptance. An OAuth authentication rejection permits at most one refresh retry, before MAIL/RCPT/DATA.

Email supplies outbound SMTP only. Continue using the existing Gmail skill for Gmail search, reads, threads, drafts, labels and mailbox operations.

Shared Google Workspace identity

For Gmail REST and future Calendar/Drive skills, use Google Workspace OAuth App and Google Workspace Account templates with auth.google_connect, auth.google_accounts and auth.google_status. Features share one verified identity and token bundle. The generic Auth and Google SMTP profiles above retain their existing contract. See Shared Google Workspace identity.
